Fix: in the abstract sentence 'characterized up to constants depending only on the interaction order and treatment probability' add an explicit clause, and in Section 1 after the displayed frontier add one sentence recording the \(2^\beta\) and \(p(1-p)\) dependence, so a reader with \(\beta\) or \(p\) drifting with \(n\) is not misled about uniformity.

The estimand and its interpretation are never given an econometric reading commensurate with the venue: \(\tau_n\) is introduced in Section 2 in one clause ('the average all-treated-versus-all-control contrast') and never connected to a policy question, and Section 4 discusses only rates. Fix: add a short paragraph in Section 1 (after the second paragraph) explaining what the all-treated-versus-all-control contrast means for a platform or market-level intervention, and why the design-based, noiseless, known-graph frame is the right idealization for that question.

Positioning is a citation list rather than a comparison: the Introduction bundles ten works into two \citep chains and asserts only that the paper 'is closest to' \citet{CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023}. Fix: replace the closing sentence of that paragraph with two or three sentences that state what SNIPE's existing variance bound delivers (an upper bound of the same \(dA_d/n\) form), and identify the delta contributed here (the matching complete-block lower bound, the exact local linear constant, and the bounded-outcome comparison), naming which of \citet{HarshawSavjeWang2025,Leung2022,Savje2021} address rates versus exposure design.

Assumption commentary repeatedly certifies each condition as 'the standard ...' with a single citation and no discussion of restrictiveness; \cref{obj:ass:low-order} in particular is the substantive modelling restriction and \cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design} rules out clustered and covariate-dependent designs common in practice. Fix: after \cref{obj:ass:low-order}, add two sentences giving a concrete setting in which bounded interaction order \(\beta\) is credible and one in which it fails (saturation or threshold exposure), and after \cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}, note which conclusions use independence essentially (the centered-monomial orthogonality) versus which would survive weaker designs.

The known-graph assumption carries the entire estimator construction — \cref{obj:def:snipe-score} evaluates \(N_i\) exactly — but the only acknowledgement is the phrase 'graph uncertainty' in the future-work list. Fix: add a paragraph to Section 4 before the Limitations paragraph stating where \(N_i\) enters (score weights and the overlap count in \cref{obj:lem:overlap-count}), and what a perturbed or over-specified neighborhood would do to unbiasedness and to the degree factor \(d\), so the reader can gauge the practical scope of the frontier.

\Cref{obj:thm:sharp-local-linear-constant-and-representers} is stated as one long theorem containing seven distinct conclusions (finite value, blockwise identity, per-block lower bound, an iff, a sufficient condition, an existence clause, and a relabeling clause), which obscures which parts are the contribution; the constant-two distance clause in particular is presented without explaining what a reader should take from it beyond non-uniqueness. Fix: split the statement into a proposition (finite-sample value and blockwise identity) and a theorem (asymptotic characterization plus the witness construction), and add one sentence before the theorem saying explicitly that the witness shows the SNIPE score is not identified by risk optimality within the local linear class.

Several notational objects are used before or without definition in the reader-facing text: \(A_i\) appears in the 'Score energy' clause of \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier} and again in \cref{obj:thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier} with no definition anywhere in Section 2, \(\Delta_r(p)\) is used in \cref{obj:def:exposed-order} and \cref{obj:def:snipe-score} with its formula appearing only inside the proof of \cref{obj:thm:fair-coin-energy-frontier}, and \(L_d\) is named in prose but never displayed. Fix: add a displayed definition of \(\Delta_r(p)=p^r-(1-p)^r\) and of the local score energy \(A_i\) immediately before \cref{obj:def:exposed-order} and \cref{obj:def:block-score-energy} respectively, and display \(L_d(f):=f(\mathbf 1)-f(\mathbf 0)\) where the block-local Riesz world is introduced.

claims_vs_assumptions: The abstract and introduction state the frontier broadly, while the formal theorem fixes beta and p and allows constants depending on them; revise those summary claims to foreground fixed beta and fixed p.

positioning: The literature paragraph lists many related strands but gives limited paper-by-paper differentiation; add 2-3 precise comparisons explaining which rates, designs, or model classes the closest papers cover.

assumption_discussion: The setup motivates bounded degree, Bernoulli assignment, and coefficient mass locally, but the Discussion should spell out what empirical settings these assumptions capture and where common-p Bernoulli randomization is the right design abstraction.
writing: The paper repeats theorem content in prose at high density, especially after each main result; shorten post-theorem paragraphs and move technical restatement into interpretation.
The bounded-outcome theorem includes a strict-containment claim with a terse example in the proof; add a short reader-facing explanation near the theorem so the envelope comparison is transparent.

The verification note asserts broad Lean coverage, but the boundary between verified algebra and econometric interpretation could be sharper; add a compact verification-scope table separating checked statements, proof sketches, and cited contextual claims.

Abstract and Introduction present the frontier as a characterization 'up to constants depending only on \((\beta,p)\)' without disclosing how badly those constants can degrade in \(\beta\): the proof of \cref{obj:lem:block-energy-representer} takes \(c_2:=2^\beta\sum_{r\le\beta}e_r(p)\) and \(H:=c_1+2^\beta\sum_r m_r(p)/c_1\), both exponential in \(\beta\), and \(c_1\) is a minimum of \(\Delta_r(p)^2/[p(1-p)]^r\) that blows up as \(p\to0\) or \(p\to1\). Fix: add one sentence at the end of the Introduction's main-result paragraph stating the explicit \((\beta,p)\) dependence of \(c_{\beta,p},C_{\beta,p}\) implied by the construction (exponential in \(\beta\), degenerate as \(p(1-p)\to0\)), and note that the sharpness claim is therefore a statement for fixed \((\beta,p)\) with the ratio \(C_{\beta,p}/c_{\beta,p}\) not tracked.

The abstract's headline sentence 'the minimax mean squared error is characterized' and the Discussion sentence 'the minimax comparison measures the exact price of estimating the total treatment effect' overstate relative to \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier}, which delivers matching orders with unequal constants, not an exact value; only the complete-block local linear benchmark \(B^2A_{d_t}/m_t\) and the canonical-SNIPE block risk are exact. Fix: replace 'exact price' with 'the order of the price' in the paragraph following \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier}, and in the abstract write 'determined up to \((\beta,p)\)-dependent constants' rather than 'characterized'.

The assumption commentary is a sequence of four near-identical paragraphs that each assert the condition is 'the standard ... condition \citep{CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023}' without interpreting what it rules out substantively: no discussion of why common-probability Bernoulli (rather than cluster or saturation designs) is the right benchmark, what economic settings make bounded in- AND out-degree plausible (out-degree is the substantive restriction, and it is stated but never motivated), how \(\beta\) would be known in practice, or that outcomes are noiseless deterministic functions of \(z\) — a strong restriction relegated to a single clause in the Limitations paragraph. Fix: expand \cref{obj:ass:bounded-degree} and \cref{obj:ass:low-order} commentary with one substantive paragraph each giving an applied setting where the bound holds and one where it plausibly fails (e.g. hub-heavy social graphs violate out-degree bounds), and promote the noiseless-outcome restriction into the Setup with a sentence explaining that all randomness is design randomness.

Positioning relative to \citet{CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023} is asserted rather than demonstrated: the Introduction says the paper 'sharpens that known-graph Bernoulli setting by deriving matched minimax upper and lower bounds with explicit degree dependence', but never states what variance bound SNIPE already carried in that paper, so the reader cannot see which half is new (the lower bound and the local linear benchmark, presumably) versus recovered. The remaining citations \citep{HarshawSavjeWang2025,EichhornKhanUganderYu2026,WangLi2026,Leung2022,Savje2021,Hu2022,Gao2025} appear only in undifferentiated bundles with no claim attached to any individual one. Fix: add two or three sentences to the related-work paragraph recording the specific prior upper bound in the SNIPE paper and its degree dependence, and replace at least the \citet{HarshawSavjeWang2025} and \citet{Leung2022} bundle mentions with one-clause statements of what each does differently (design, estimand, or asymptotic regime).

The definitional apparatus in the Setup is unusually heavy — sixteen definitions, four of them auto-named \texttt{synth\_1}--\texttt{synth\_4} in a way that leaks pipeline internals into reader-facing labels — and three of them (\cref{obj:synth_3,obj:synth_4} for \(\Pi_\pm\), \cref{obj:def:zero-degree-conventions}) restate content already fixed by \cref{obj:def:block-family}. Fix: rename the \texttt{synth\_k} environments to descriptive ids, fold the \(\Pi_+\) and \(\Pi_-\) definitions into a single remark immediately after \cref{obj:def:block-family}, and move \cref{obj:def:zero-degree-conventions} to a footnote or appendix so the Setup reads as a model description rather than a symbol table.

\Cref{obj:thm:sharp-local-linear-constant-and-representers} is stated as one theorem carrying six distinct conclusions (finite-sample value, blockwise identity, per-block lower bound, iff characterization, sufficiency of score closeness, and an existence construction with normalized distance exactly \(2\)), which makes the headline claim hard to extract, and the paper never explains why the constant is exactly \(2\) or what the \(L^2\) distance of \(2\) means in interpretable terms (it is the maximum for unit-normalized orthogonal deviations, a point worth stating). Fix: split into a proposition (finite-sample value plus \(\Psi_{b,t}\) identity and per-block bound) and a theorem (the iff plus the non-uniqueness witness), and add one interpretive sentence after the theorem explaining that distance \(2\) corresponds to a perturbation orthogonal to the score with energy equal to the score's own, i.e. the maximal separation compatible with asymptotic optimality.

The Discussion contributes little beyond restating the theorems: its first four paragraphs re-narrate the \(dA_d/n\) decomposition, the complete-block benchmark, and the bounded-outcome extension in the same terms already used in the Introduction, and the Limitations paragraph is a bare list of five extensions with no indication of which are within reach of the present technique. Fix: cut the redundant restatement to one paragraph and replace it with the missing practical content — what the frontier implies for choosing \(p\) or for the sample size needed at a given \(d\) (e.g. consistency requires \(d\binom{d}{k_\star}=o(n)\), a strong restriction worth stating explicitly), and say which of the listed extensions the block Riesz argument would plausibly carry over to.

The proof architecture appears circular: the proof of \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier} invokes \cref{obj:thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier}, while the prose following \cref{obj:thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier} says it uses \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier} to convert energy to the binomial scale; revise the appendix and theorem discussion to state a one-way dependency order clearly.

Several claims state broad econometric positioning without enough specificity, especially references to related low-order, clustered, and covariate-adjusted interference estimators in the introduction and discussion; add one sentence per cited cluster explaining the exact comparison target, such as assignment regime, estimand, graph knowledge, or estimator class.

The assumption discussion motivates bounded degree, low order, and coefficient mass, but the restrictiveness of known graph, common-probability Bernoulli assignment, noiseless observation, fixed beta, and fixed p is concentrated late in the limitations paragraph; move concise affirmative scope statements into Setup or Introduction so readers see the operating regime before the main theorem.

There are cross-reference contract violations in theorem statements and proofs where \cref commands are placed inside math mode, for example `\(\cref{obj:def:exposed-order,...}\)`; use text-mode `\cref{...}` consistently unless the reference itself is part of a displayed formula.

The local linear theorem is dense and mixes exact finite-sample risk, asymptotic equivalence, non-uniqueness, and relabeling invariance in one long statement; split the theorem or add a short roadmap paragraph before it that names the three outputs: exact value, excess criterion, and non-uniqueness of optimal weights.

The bounded-outcome theorem’s model-comparison clause says strict containment is witnessed by coefficients `B` and `-2B`, but the paper gives no intuitive explanation of how the resulting outcomes remain uniformly bounded by `B`; add a short verification sentence or choose a simpler witness whose bounded-outcome property is transparent.

The abstract and Introduction both assert the frontier is characterized "up to constants depending only on $(\beta,p)$" and "uniform in $n$, $d$, and $B$," but the formal statement of \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier} restricts to $d\le n$ and $B\ge0$ with $\beta\ge1$ fixed, and the sharp constant claims in the lower branch rest on a $\min\{1,\cdot\}$ that is trivially saturated once $d\binom{d}{k_\star}\ge n$. In that saturated regime the theorem asserts only $c_{\beta,p}B^2\le R_n^\star\le C_{\beta,p}B^2$, which is a statement about a bounded target rather than a rate characterization. Fix: in the abstract and in the paragraph introducing the frontier in Section 1, state the two regimes explicitly ("for $d\binom{d}{k_\star}\le n$ the frontier is $B^2 d\binom{d}{k_\star}/n$; beyond that threshold the risk is of order $B^2$ and no consistent estimation of $\tau_n$ at the stated scale is characterized"), and carry the $d\le n$, $\beta\ge1$ conditions into the first prose sentence stating the result.

$k_\star(d,\beta,p)$ is presented in the abstract and Introduction as "the maximum $r$ whose Bernoulli all-treated-versus-all-control contrast is nonzero," but nothing in the reader-facing text explains why the *maximum* exposed order (rather than, say, the sum over exposed orders, which is what $A_d$ actually is) sets the rate; the connection is buried in the constants $c_1,c_2$ of \cref{obj:lem:block-energy-representer}, where the upper bound uses $\binom{d}{r}\le 2^\beta\binom{d}{k}$. Fix: add two or three sentences after the display in Section 1 (the paragraph beginning "The proof identifies two finite-design objects") explaining that for fixed $\beta$ the sum $\sum_r\binom{d}{r}\Delta_r^2/[p(1-p)]^r$ is dominated within a $(\beta,p)$-dependent factor by its largest exposed term, so $A_d\asymp_{\beta,p}\binom{d}{k_\star}$ — and note explicitly that the implied constants degrade with $\beta$ (they contain $2^\beta$ and $[p(1-p)]^{-\beta}$), so the characterization is a fixed-$(\beta,p)$ statement and not uniform as $\beta$ grows or $p\to\{0,1\}$.

Section 2 ("Setup and Assumptions") states each assumption and then, in a one- or two-sentence follow-up, calls it "the standard" condition with a citation to \citet{CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023}, but never discusses restrictiveness. In particular: (i) the known-graph requirement is load-bearing for the entire estimator, since $g_{i,\beta,p}$ is built from $N_i$, yet it appears only as "a known directed graph $G_n$ records interference"; (ii) potential outcomes are exactly polynomial and noiseless, so the model has no idiosyncratic error term at all, which is a strong departure from most applied design-based settings; (iii) the coefficient-mass envelope \cref{obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass} is an $\ell_1$ restriction on coefficients, not on outcomes, and its economic content is left implicit. Fix: after \cref{obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}, add a paragraph interpreting each condition substantively — what an $\ell_1$ coefficient budget means for the magnitude of realized spillovers, what noiselessness buys in the risk calculation, and which conditions the results are known to use only through the exposed-order and overlap counts — and cross-reference the Limitations paragraph so a reader meets the restrictiveness discussion at the point of assumption rather than eight pages later.

The abstract's claim that "asymptotic optimality is characterized by a blockwise quadratic excess criterion" overstates the scope of \cref{obj:thm:sharp-local-linear-constant-and-representers}: the characterization is of asymptotic attainment of the *local linear* benchmark $B^2A_{d_t}/m_t$ within the moment-restricted class $\mathcal E_t^{\mathrm{loc,lin}}$ on a *complete-block* graph sequence with $d_t\mid n_t$, not asymptotic optimality among estimators generally. The same slippage occurs in the Introduction ("proves that its excess over $d_t^2A_{d_t}$ exactly characterizes asymptotic attainment of the benchmark") and in the Discussion ("necessary and sufficient for asymptotic minimaxity inside the local linear class" is correct, but the preceding sentence in the Discussion calls the block calculation the criterion "that any asymptotically optimal local linear rule must match," which reads as unconditional). Fix: in the abstract write "On complete-block graph sequences with $d_t\mid n_t$, the local linear benchmark has exact finite-sample value $B^2A_{d_t}/m_t$, and attainment of that benchmark within the moment-restricted local linear class is characterized by a blockwise quadratic excess criterion"; make the same three qualifiers (complete blocks, divisibility, class restriction) explicit at each of the three prose sites.

The Setup section is organized as an uninterrupted run of nineteen numbered environments with only one- or two-sentence connectives, and four of them carry non-descriptive labels (\cref{obj:synth_1}, \cref{obj:synth_2}, \cref{obj:synth_3}, \cref{obj:synth_4}) whose rendered cross-references give the reader no indication of what object is being cited; two of these ($\Pi_+$, $\Pi_-$) also restate content already fixed by \cref{obj:def:block-family}, and $\Pi_-$ appears before $\Pi_+$. Fix: rename the four synthetic labels to descriptive ids in the object-registry convention used elsewhere (e.g. \texttt{def:design-l2-space}, \texttt{def:block-poly-space}, \texttt{def:block-prior-plus}, \texttt{def:block-prior-minus}), reorder $\Pi_+$ before $\Pi_-$, and collapse the two signed-prior definitions into a single environment parameterized by $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}$ that references \cref{obj:def:block-family} rather than repeating the schedule.

Positioning relies on a single sentence — "The present paper sharpens that known-graph Bernoulli setting by deriving matched minimax upper and lower bounds with explicit degree dependence" — to distinguish the contribution from \citet{CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023}, without stating what that paper establishes. A reader cannot tell whether the antecedent gives a variance bound, a rate, or a one-sided minimax statement, and therefore cannot verify that the delta claimed here is real. The five 2025--2026 citations (\citealt{HarshawSavjeWang2025,EichhornKhanUganderYu2026,WangLi2026}) are likewise invoked three times as a block with no individual content. Fix: expand the Introduction's related-work paragraph to state in one sentence each what the SNIPE paper proves (its estimator, its variance/rate result, and whether any lower bound is present) and what each of the three recent papers contributes, then state the delta as a comparison of specific objects; if any citation's content cannot be stated specifically, drop it rather than listing it.

The \paragraph{Limitations and future work} at the end of the Discussion lists five extensions ("alternative randomization schemes, covariate adjustment, graph uncertainty, clustered assignment, and sampling or outcome noise") without indicating which are close-at-hand versus structural obstacles to the present method, which weakens its informativeness. In particular, outcome noise and graph uncertainty are not symmetric with the others: the SNIPE score's unbiasedness survives additive mean-zero noise with an inflated variance, whereas the score is built from $N_i$ and has no obvious analogue under an unknown graph. Fix: replace the flat list with two or three sentences that separate extensions preserving the block Riesz structure (noise, unequal $p_j$, covariate adjustment applied to the baseline coefficients) from those requiring a different construction (graph uncertainty, clustered assignment, which breaks the independence in \cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design}), and state affirmatively for each which of the paper's two ingredients — block energy or overlap count — would need replacing.

Two internal presentational inconsistencies will confuse a careful reader. First, the projection interval differs across the two classes ($[-B,B]$ in \cref{obj:def:snipe-estimator} versus $[-2B,2B]$ in \cref{obj:def:bounded-outcome-clipped-snipe}), yet step 5 of the \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier} proof shows $|\tau_n|\le 2B$ on the coefficient-mass class — so the coefficient-mass projection clips to an interval strictly smaller than the range of the target it estimates, which reads as an error even though the risk bound still goes through (the proof absorbs it via the $9B^2$ saturated bound). Second, $A_i$ is introduced mid-paragraph in Section 2, inside the prose describing the block Riesz world, rather than as a numbered definition, though it appears in the statement of \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier}. Fix: add one sentence after \cref{obj:def:snipe-estimator} explaining why clipping to $[-B,B]$ is deliberate on the coefficient-mass class (or widen it to $[-2B,2B]$ for consistency), and promote $A_i$ to a short numbered definition immediately before \cref{obj:def:block-score-energy} so that every symbol in the main theorem has an anchored referent.

The verification appendix asserts that "the theorem statements and their proofs are machine-checked in Lean 4" for an enumerated list of components, but the enumeration is by paper object rather than by Lean declaration, and the proofs in the deferred-proofs appendix carry inline `% lean:` comments naming declarations (e.g. `degree_frontier`, `completeBlock_all_risks_exact`, `orthogonalWitness_normalized_relabel_distance_eq_two`) that are invisible to the reader. A referee cannot map claims to checked artifacts. Fix: in the Verification Note, add a table with one row per numbered result giving the Lean declaration name and the file, state which axioms/`sorry`-freedom holds, and say explicitly that the bibliographic and interpretive content in Sections 1 and 3 is not part of the checked development.

Introduction/abstract: several claims present the frontier as broadly minimax before restating all gates. Suggested fix: in the first sentence of each result summary, include the full design scope: fixed finite population, known bounded in/out degree, common-p Bernoulli assignment, fixed beta, coefficient-mass or bounded-outcome envelope.

Bounded-outcome theorem discussion: the phrase 'bounded-outcome lower frontier is inherited' risks overstating what is established because the displayed lower bound is for the coefficient-mass risk and transfers through class inclusion. Suggested fix: state affirmatively that class inclusion supplies the displayed lower bound for the bounded-outcome comparison through the ordered risks.

Positioning paragraph in the introduction: citations to broad interference and recent low-order work are plausible but sometimes generic. Suggested fix: add one clause per closest paper identifying the precise contrast: known-graph Bernoulli SNIPE, degree-sensitive variance, clustered/covariate-adjusted setting, etc.

Setup and assumptions: assumptions are individually interpreted, but the combined restrictiveness is concentrated only in the final limitations paragraph. Suggested fix: add a short setup paragraph explaining why common-p Bernoulli assignment, known graph, noiseless schedules, and fixed beta form the target design regime.

Main results: the local linear benchmark section is technically clear but dense; the reader reaches the criterion before receiving enough intuition for the estimator class. Suggested fix: add a short paragraph before the theorem explaining that the benchmark restricts weights to block-local moment-correcting linear rules on complete-block sequences.

Writing: the draft repeats long theorem paraphrases after already lengthy formal statements, especially after the bounded-outcome theorem. Suggested fix: shorten post-theorem prose to the interpretation of the rate, estimator, and block construction, moving proof-roadmap details to the appendix.

The stated minimax risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} takes the infimum over all estimators measurable with respect to (G_n, Z, Y^obs), but item 5 of the proof of \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier} must verify that the clipped SNIPE estimator is 'admissible' and has uniformly bounded risk before concluding R_n^\star is below its worst risk — an admissibility restriction that appears in \cref{obj:def:two-class-minimax-risks} for R_{n,\infty}^\star (bounded risk range) but not in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}. Fix: state one estimator class once, with the boundedness condition made explicit in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, and add a sentence justifying why the restriction is imposed and why R_{n,\ell_1}^\star \le R_{n,\infty}^\star still compares like with like when the two infima range over differently restricted estimator sets.

The two computations that actually produce the result are asserted rather than argued. In the proof of \cref{obj:thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier}, item 4 writes the unclipped SNIPE bound B^2 dA_d/n in one sentence ('the unclipped SNIPE variance calculation, with the local dependence aggregation controlled by \cref{obj:lem:overlap-count}, yields...'), and item 8 asserts H^2(\Pi_+,\Pi_-) \le 4\pi^2 m\delta^2/(B^2A_d) with no derivation; both carry only Lean tags. Fix: display the covariance expansion of Var(\widehat\tau_n^{SNIPE}) over centered monomial pairs and the point at which \cref{obj:lem:overlap-count} is applied, and give the per-block Hellinger computation for the cos^2 density showing where 4\pi^2 comes from. Relatedly, item 5 of the proof of \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier} justifies clipping to [-B,B] using the bound |\tau_n| \le 2B, which does not justify that interval; replace it with the sharper display \tau_n = n^{-1}\sum_i \sum_{S\ne\varnothing} c_{i,S}, hence |\tau_n| \le B under \cref{obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass}, which is also what explains the different interval [-2B,2B] in \cref{obj:def:bounded-outcome-clipped-snipe}.

The 'local linear benchmark' is presented in the abstract and introduction without the restrictions that give it its value: \cref{obj:def:local-linear-estimator-class} imposes exact blockwise mean-zero and unit raw-monomial moment conditions for every nonempty S, so R_t^{loc,lin} is a restricted-unbiased minimax value, not the minimax value over graph-local estimators generally. Moreover B^2A_{d_t}/m_t diverges when A_{d_t}/m_t \to \infty while \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier} caps the unrestricted minimax risk at C_{\beta,p}B^2, so the benchmark is attained only in the unsaturated regime. Fix: in the abstract and in the paragraph introducing \cref{obj:thm:sharp-local-linear-constant-and-representers}, name the class as exactly-unbiased block-local weights, and add one sentence after the theorem recording that the benchmark is informative when dA_d/n \lesssim 1 and that clipping is what delivers the capped rate outside that regime.

Each of \cref{obj:ass:bernoulli-design,obj:ass:bounded-degree,obj:ass:low-order,obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass} is followed by a single sentence calling it 'standard' with a citation to \citet{CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023}, and the Limitations paragraph only lists the conditions again. Substantive restrictiveness is never engaged: the graph is known exactly, potential outcomes are noiseless (so the entire lower bound must be generated by randomizing the coefficient schedule, which deserves a comment), the out-degree bound rules out hub structures typical of observed social networks, and the common-p requirement excludes covariate- or degree-dependent propensities. Fix: add a paragraph after \cref{obj:ass:bounded-coefficient-mass} interpreting each condition substantively — what an analyst must know or verify, which empirical designs satisfy it, and how the frontier would be expected to move if it fails.

The (\beta,p) dependence of the constants is never described, although the proof of \cref{obj:lem:block-energy-representer} makes it explicit: c_2 = 2^\beta \sum_r \Delta_r(p)^2 [p(1-p)]^{-r}, so C_{\beta,p} grows exponentially in \beta and blows up as p \to 0 or 1, and H likewise. The abstract's 'characterized up to constants depending only on (\beta,p)' and 'the implied constants are uniform in n, d, and B' therefore read as stronger uniformity than is delivered — and uniformity in B is trivial given the exact B^2 scaling. Fix: state the explicit constant formulas in a remark after \cref{obj:thm:degree-frontier} and add one sentence in the abstract or introduction recording that the frontier is a fixed-(\beta,p) statement whose constants degrade exponentially in \beta and polynomially in [p(1-p)]^{-\beta}, so \beta and d cannot be traded off freely.

Presentation of the setup and positioning both need tightening. (i) Four definitions carry auto-generated labels that leak into the reader-facing text — \cref{obj:synth_1} is cited in the discussion after \cref{obj:lem:block-energy-representer} — and \Pi_+ and \Pi_- are each redefined in synth_3 and synth_4 although \cref{obj:def:block-family} already defines \Pi_\sigma for both signs; H_{\beta,p} := \sup_{d\ge1}\sum_T |h_{d,T}| is used to define \delta before the coefficient-envelope clause of \cref{obj:lem:block-energy-representer} establishes that the supremum is finite. Fix: give the four definitions descriptive labels, delete synth_3 and synth_4 in favour of a one-line 'write \Pi_\pm for \Pi_\sigma with \sigma = \pm 1', and add a forward pointer to the lemma at the definition of H_{\beta,p}. (ii) The literature appears mainly as undifferentiated citation blocks (Sobel2006 through Gao2025 in one bracket) and the comparison to the closest antecedent stays qualitative. Fix: state in the introduction what variance bound \citet{CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023} establish, in what form, and how its order compares numerically to dA_d/n, and add one or two sentences on whether any matching lower bound or impossibility result already exists in the interference literature.

Introduction, paragraph beginning “The coefficient-mass model has a bounded-outcome analogue”: the phrase “equivalent frontier” blurs the distinction between the coefficient-mass and bounded-outcome classes; revise to state that both classes are governed by the same energy scale under the theorem’s fixed-β, fixed-p, bounded-degree conditions.

Setup, bounded-degree and Bernoulli-assignment discussion: the assumptions are described as standard, but their substantive implications are only lightly interpreted; add 2-3 sentences explaining what common-p Bernoulli assignment and known graph neighborhoods buy analytically and which experimental designs they cover.
